blocks.text: On user-defined networks, Docker runs a DNS server at 127.0.0.11 in each container that resolves container names, Compose service names and aliases, and forwards everything else upstream.

$ docker compose exec api cat /etc/resolv.conf
nameserver 127.0.0.11

items: Names resolve only between containers sharing a network; a container on two networks resolves both.
Stopped containers drop out of DNS: "name not resolved" can just mean the target is down.
Several containers with one name (`--scale worker=3`) → all IPs returned (round-robin, no health awareness).

blocks.text: IPs change on recreate. A client that resolves once keeps using the dead IP. nginx `proxy_pass http://api:8000` resolves at startup → 502 after api is recreated.
Connection pools have the same issue: use pre-ping and retries.
`container_name:` is rarely needed. The service name already resolves, and a fixed name blocks scaling and collides across projects.

Q: "Why does nginx return 502 after the backend container is recreated?" A: "nginx resolved the backend name once at startup and cached the old IP. Point resolver at 127.0.0.11 and use a variable upstream so it re-resolves, or reload nginx after deploys."

items: Resolution needs a shared network and a running target.
Clients that cache DNS break on recreate.
